newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan SEC says no move to dampen stock markets.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan SEC says no move to dampen stock markets.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Thursday it has no intention to dampen the stock market after recent rises.
"We have no intention to dampen the markets," a commisison spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.

On Wednesday, the main TAIEX index ended down 1.99 percent at 7,730.49, dragged down by profit-taking against big recent gains in electronics and a sharp downturn in the fledgling over-the-counter exchange, brokers said.
Brokers attributed the OTC fall and, in turn, the TAIEX's, to the Securities and Exchange Commission's rejection on Tuesday of Capital Securities' planned T$800 million OTC rights issue.
The spokeswoman said the rejection was an isolated case and the issue was rejected because Capital did not offer satisfactory documents.
"Disapproval of a single case does not mean we intend to dampen the markets. That was simply speculation," she said.
Late on Wednesday, the commission approved Jih-Sun Securities' application to raise a securities trust fund of up to T$10 billion, she said.
The commission also approved applications by two foreign funds to remit US$200 million each into the two local stock markets, she said.
